label: token right after a "2" early in the original sequence (positions 2-4)
explanation: Fires in the original (input) phase on the step right after the digit 2 was input, when that step is position 2-4. 96% of activation mass has prev_tok == 2; t=2-4 holds ~99% of mass. Never fires at t=0-1, almost never at t>=5, never in the copy phase, and only weakly at the delimiter. The current input token does not matter. Strongest activations (~0.95-1.0 of max) come at t=3 after a 2 at position 2, often with a digit or another 2 earlier and a first token of a/e/f; those first tokens have the highest rates (lift about 2.3x). Activation stays lower when the 2 sits at position 0-1 and the feature fires at t=2 (second 2 in examples like e 2 [2]). Missed activations are mostly weak (lowest quartile) and come after other digits (0/1/3) at the same positions; these hold 4% of mass. False positives are mostly at t=4 after a 2 at position 3 with letter-only prefixes.

issues: The core claims hold. Phase shares on dev are original 0.998, delimiter 0.002, copy 0 (zero active steps). It never fires at t=0-1. The t=2-4 window holds 99.4% of the mass, t=5 holds 0.6%, and t>=6 only 4 steps. prev_tok==2 holds 96.4% of the mass (lift 29x). The current input token barely matters (in_tok lifts 1.1-1.4x). Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.882, R 0.802, F1 0.840, mass recall 0.959.

Precision falls with position. prev_tok==2 gives P 1.00 at t=2, 0.97 at t=3, 0.63 at t=4 and 0.09 at t=5. The t=4 term is a weak, partly unreliable edge of the window and could be stated more clearly. Dropping it (t<=3) raises test P to 0.986 but cuts F1 to 0.77, so keeping it is right.

Wrong secondary claim: 'missed activations are mainly after other digits (0/1/3)'. Predicate (phase==0)&(prev_tok!=2)&(t in 2..5)&prev_tok in DIGITS covers only 2.6% of active steps, while the missed set is about 18% of active steps and mostly follows letters (h, o, t, g...). Each of those letters has lift 1.0x or less, so the misses are scattered and weak (lowest-quartile coverage 0.29) rather than a pattern. A 'lingering' class (2 two steps back) is also not a real class: P 0.09, mass 2.2%.

Questionable claim: 'false positives are mostly at t=4 after a 2 with all-letter prefixes'. At t=4, precision is actually lower when the earlier prefix contains another digit (0.57) than when the 2 is the only digit so far (0.66). The all-letter case may supply more FPs by count only because it is more common.

Small systematic false-positive class: first_tok==2 with another 2 at position 2 (t=3) fires only 17% of the time, but it covers 0.03% of the mass. Excluding it lifts test F1 only from 0.840 to 0.843, which is not material.
The label is ambiguous: 'positions 2-4' means the current step t, so the 2 itself sits at positions 1-3. The explanation states this correctly.
skeptic.revised_label: Original-phase step right after a '2' input, at steps t=2-4 (the 2 at positions 1-3); strongest at t=2-3, unreliable at t=4

final_label: Original-phase step right after a '2' input, at steps t=2-4 (the 2 at positions 1-3); strongest at t=2-3, unreliable at t=4
